paper_title: DLP Dynamic Layerwise Pruning in Large Language Models
caption_used: Comparison of per-output and per-layer perplexity at different sparsity rates using a logarithmic scale. Both pruning configurations maintain comparable perplexity below 10^1 for sparsity rates up to 50%, after which values begin to diverge. At 60% sparsity, the Per-Output configuration reaches approximately 15 while Per-Layer remains near 10^1. The most pronounced separation occurs at 70%, where Per-Output perplexity climbs to roughly 50 while Per-Layer reaches approximately 25. At 80% sparsity, both configurations approach 10^3, with Per-Output exhibiting marginally higher perplexity than Per-Layer at this extreme.

model_annotations.Bulgarian: This bar graph titled "Comparison of per-output and per-layer perplexity at different sparsity rates" illustrates the relationship between sparsity rate and perplexity on a logarithmic scale for two different pruning configurations: per-output and per-layer. The logarithmic scale is represented on the y-axis, labeled "Perplexity", and the sparsity rate is represented on the x-axis, with values ranging from 10% to 80%. There are two sets of bars for each sparsity rate: the blue bars represent the per-output perplexity, and the orange bars represent the per-layer perplexity. As the sparsity rate increases, both perplexity values generally increase, but they exhibit different trends. At lower sparsity rates, the perplexities are relatively similar, both being below 10^1. However, as the sparsity rate rises above 50%, the perplexity values begin to diverge, with the per-output perplexity increasing at a faster rate than the per-layer perplexity. At 60% sparsity, the per-output perplexity reaches approximately 15, while the per-layer perplexity remains just below 10^1. The most significant difference is observed at 70% sparsity, where the per-output perplexity is about 50, compared to 25 for per-layer, and by 80% sparsity, the per-output perplexity is approaching 10^3, slightly higher than the per-layer perplexity. This graph does not include any legends, so no further interpretation is provided beyond the data represented.
model_annotations.Chinese: The bar chart compares two different configurations in terms of perplexity across various sparsity rates measured at 0%, 10%, 20%, 30%, 40%, 50%, 60%, 70%, and 80%. Perplexity is quantified on a logarithmic scale, with the x-axis representing sparsity rate and the y-axis indicating perplexity on a logarithmic scale from 10² to 10³. Per-Output is represented by orange bars, and Per-Layer by blue bars. At a 10% sparsity rate, both configurations have perplexity values below 10^1. As sparsity increases to 50%, perplexity for both remains below 10^1. Between 50% and 60% sparsity, Per-Output shows a higher propensity for perplexity, slightly above 15, compared to Per-Layer, which is maintained near 10^1. A substantial increase in perplexity is observed at 70% sparsity, where Per-Output perplexity rises to around 50, whereas Per-Layer perplexity is approximately 25. At the highest level of sparsity at 80%, both allocations show perplexity at approximately 10^3, with Per-Output being slightly higher than Per-Layer.
model_annotations.English: This bar chart compares the perplexity of per-output and per-layer configurations during sparsity rates of large language models. The horizontal axis represents sparsity rates at increments of 10%, ranging from 10% to 80%. The vertical axis uses a logarithmic scale to measure perplexity, starting from 10^1 to 10^3. Per-layer perplexity is depicted in orange and begins below 10^1 for sparsity rates up to 50%. At 60% sparsity, per-layer perplexity is approximately 10^1, and at 70% it slightly increases to around 25. At 80%, per-layer perplexity is close to 10^3. Per-output perplexity is shown in blue: it starts below 10^1 at 10% sparsity and is also below 10^1 for rates up to 50%. At 60% sparsity, per-output perplexity is around 15, at 70% it significantly rises to about 50, and at 80% it approaches 10^3. The gap between the two configurations widens notably at 70% and 80% sparsity rates.
model_annotations.German: Das diagramm veranschaulicht die Perplexität auf verschiedenen Stärkenraten unter Berücksichtigung von Per-Output und Per-Layer Pruning. Es verwendet eine logarithmische Skalierung für die Perplexität an den Y-Achsen, wobei die X-Achse Stärkenraten von 10% bis 80% vorstellt. Für jede Stärkenrate werden zwei Balken dargestellt, die die Perplexität für Per-Output und Per-Layer darstellen; Per-Output ist in Blau und Per-Layer in Orange dargestellt. Bis zu einer Stärkenrate von 50% nähren sich sowohl Per-Output als auch Per-Layer am gleichen Punkt an, wobei sich ihre Werte mit zunehmender Stärkenrate auseinandersprechen. Das bemerkenswerteste Muster tritt bei 70% Stärkenrate auf, wo Per-Output eine signifikant höhere Perplexität aufweist, während Per-Layer seine Werte deutlich niedriger hat. Das Layout, die Beschriftungen und die vergleichende Form der Balken bieten Einblicke in die unterschiedlichen Auswirkungen von Per-Output und Per-Layer Pruning auf die Perplexität. Es ist wichtig zu beachten, dass die Grafik keinen Vergleich zwischen Per-Output und Per-Layer auf Stärkenraten niedriger als 50% liefert und die Informationen relativistisch sind; obwohl die Perplexität bei höheren Stärkenraten ähnlich wird, lässt diese Divergenz die Komplexität und das dynamische Verhalten der Pruning-Funktionen bei variablen Stärkenraten hervorheben.
